title: TEMAIRAZU lowers its maximum estimate of people whose data may have been exposed after forensic probe, Daily Security reports
date_note: Day the company announced its final investigation results, per Daily Security (Korea), published 25 Nov 2026; the original company notice was not read.
summary: Daily Security (Korea) reports that Japanese accommodation reservation management provider TEMAIRAZU lowered the maximum number of customers whose information may have been exposed, after an external forensic investigation. The company says the actual number of leaked individuals has not been confirmed. The probe found an access attempt on 26 August and an actual intrusion on 21 September.
plain: A Japanese hotel-booking system provider lowered its upper estimate of how many people had reservation data possibly exposed. The actual number of leaked people is not confirmed.
exec: Customers of lodging operators using this system may have had reservation data exposed; the company has lowered its upper estimate.
action: Daily Security reports TEMAIRAZU urges anyone asked to re-enter card details or pay extra for a Japanese hotel booking to verify via the booking app or the hotel's official contact first.

sources.name: Daily Security (Korea): Japan accommodation reservation system hack, possible exposure cut to up to 1 million

validation.note: Only Daily Security (Korea) read, relaying the company's announcement of 24 Nov; the company's own notice was not found or read.

evidence.quote: 일본 숙박 예약 관리업체 테마이라즈(TEMAIRAZU)가 해킹으로 노출됐을 가능성이 있는 고객 정보의 범위를 당초 최대 약 445만 명에서 최대 약 100만 명으로 줄였다.
외부 포렌식 조사에서 8월 26일 접근 시도와 9월 21일 실제 침입이 각각 확인됐다.

review.note: action said no advice though article gives user advice; now sourced. Figures, dates, no confirmed leak checked
